findings.quote: In the Bull case (25% probability, implied $60), FY2027 revenue reaches the top of the $65.0 billion to $72.0 billion guidance, the Q4'26 gross margin of 17.5% proves representative, and audited results clear the review; the stock re-rates toward its 52-week high of $58.78.
findings.issue: The scenarioCommentary re-narrates all three scenario drivers almost verbatim from the scenarios[] array, which the page already renders. The Bull sentence here duplicates scenarios[0].driver ($65-72B guidance, 17.5% GM proving representative, review cleared, re-rate to $58.78); the Base and Bear sentences likewise restate scenarios[1] and scenarios[2]. Under rubric item 7, each scenario should be argued once, not restated in two places. Only the final two sentences (blended fair value modestly above $41.44, target range brackets Base, reward/risk below the Buy bar) add anything the scenario cards do not.
findings.fix: Cut the driver-by-driver restatement and let scenarioCommentary do the work the cards cannot: argue why the probabilities are 25/50/25, reconcile the ~$44.5 probability-weighted fair value and the $37-$52 band to the current price, and state the reward/risk conclusion. Refer back to each scenario in words rather than repeating its driver text.
findings.note: Rewritten. The commentary no longer restates the driver text; it now argues the 25/50/25 weights, reconciles the ~$44.50 weighted fair value and the $37-$52 band to the $41.44 price, and states the reward/risk conclusion, referring to each scenario in words ('durable margin recovery paired with a clean audit', 'a restatement, a financing squeeze, or a large-customer pullback').

findings.quote: Management guides FY2027 net sales to a range of $65.0 billion to $72.0 billion and cites more than $60 billion in new orders and backlog entering fiscal 2027.
findings.issue: The press release attaches the $60 billion figure to new orders specifically ('generated more than $60 billion in new orders, and booked record backlog entering fiscal 2027') — backlog is described separately as 'record' and is not quantified. Here and in analystCommentary ('more than $60 billion in new orders and backlog entering fiscal 2027') the figure is attached to the broader quantity 'new orders and backlog.' The report is also internally inconsistent: sections.executiveSummary.thesis.body and finalRecommendation.body[0] correctly write 'more than $60 billion in new orders.'
findings.fix: Attach the $60B figure to new orders only, matching the press release and the report's own thesis/final-recommendation wording. If backlog is mentioned alongside, present it as separate 'record backlog' (unquantified on the grounding surface) rather than folding it into the $60B.
findings.note: growth.points[1] now reads 'more than $60 billion in new orders generated over the past year' and analystCommentary now reads 'cites more than $60 billion in new orders'. The $60B is attached to new orders only, matching the press release and the thesis/final-recommendation wording; backlog is no longer folded in. Consistent across all four fields.

findings.quote: The investment question is whether Supermicro can turn extraordinary top-line growth into durable profit and cash.
findings.issue: House style bans hype vocabulary and unearned superlatives, asking the numbers to carry the weight. 'extraordinary top-line growth' here, and 'FY2026 was a year of exceptional growth' in finalRecommendation.body[0], are hype adjectives layered on the 77.8% figure that already speaks for itself.
findings.fix: Drop 'extraordinary' and 'exceptional' and let the 77.8% growth figure stand on its own (e.g. 'turn 77.8% top-line growth into durable profit and cash').
findings.note: 'extraordinary' in thesis.body and 'exceptional' in finalRecommendation.body[0] are both replaced with the neutral 'rapid'; the 77.8% figure carries the weight. Hype vocabulary removed.

findings.quote: The durability question is whether DCBBS and a richer enterprise mix can lift margins durably, as the Q4'26 gross margin of 17.5% hints, or whether competitive pricing keeps full-year margin near 11%.
findings.issue: The exact figure 'Q4'26 gross margin of 17.5%' is repeated across many fields — analystCommentary, executiveSummary.thesis.body, financials.incomeCommentary, businessMoat moatFactors[1] and durability, valuation scenarios[0].driver and scenarioCommentary, and finalRecommendation.body[1] — past the point of notice (rubric item 9 tic / item 7 refer-back). It is the crux of the bull case, so some recurrence is warranted, but the same phrase in eight places reads as a tic.
findings.fix: Introduce the 17.5% Q4'26 gross margin once where it is argued (the income commentary), then refer back in words ('the exit-quarter margin recovery', 'that 17.5% print') in the moat, scenario and recommendation sections rather than restating the figure each time.
findings.note: Cut from eight fields to five. The named durability field now refers back in words ('the exit quarter's sharp margin recovery hints'); scenarioCommentary ('a durable margin recovery') and finalRecommendation.body[1] ('the exit-quarter gross-margin recovery') also drop the figure. The remaining appearances each sit once per section with refer-back-in-words where a section would use it twice, matching rubric item 7 for a crux figure.
